subject.title: [Bug]: Codex code-mode image() serializes browser screenshot share-hint text as image_url, causing 400 and fallback

question: Should OpenClaw require an upstream Codex release with strict code-mode image validation, or also add an OpenClaw-side current-cell interception path if the app-server protocol permits one?
rationale: The root defect is in upstream code-mode normalization, while the feasibility and long-term ownership of intercepting Codex-generated current-cell output from OpenClaw are not established by the present app-server seams.

options.title: Upstream fix and version floor
options.body: Confirm or land strict validation in Codex, bump the managed dependency, and add OpenClaw integration coverage without creating a parallel image-normalization implementation.

options.title: Add OpenClaw interception
options.body: If the protocol exposes the generated output before provider submission, downgrade invalid current-cell image items in the Codex plugin as an additional defensive boundary.

options.title: Recovery-only handling
options.body: Retry the requested model after removing the invalid item, accepting that the malformed rollout entry is still produced before recovery.

recommendation.title: Upstream fix and version floor
recommendation.body: Confirm or land strict validation in Codex, bump the managed dependency, and add OpenClaw integration coverage without creating a parallel image-normalization implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged image-sanitizer and binding-recovery history makes this the strongest available owner for deciding the OpenClaw-versus-upstream boundary.
